value: A startup raises $200M to build quantum sensors -> business or science_technology? (tech content dominant -> science_technology only if capability is the hook; if it is a funding-round story without deep tech detail -> business)
FIFA bans two leagues over gambling scandal -> sports (regulation) even though gambling is a business topic
NASA contracts SpaceX to launch a Mars sample-return -> science_technology (space/tech), not business or world
OPEC+ cuts oil output after a meeting with G7 -> business, NOT world (economic-policy lens), but borderline -> business preferred
Election in a foreign country that will change tech export rules -> world (geopolitics dominant) NOT business
Olympic host city changes due to budget shortfall -> sports (event) even if money is mentioned
A new AI model is released by OpenAI; headline focuses on the model's capabilities -> science_technology; if headline focuses on OpenAI's share -> business
An earthquake destroys a factory in Chile -> world (disaster), NOT business
Apple unveils new iPhone with a new GPU; article details the chip architecture -> science_technology; if it details price and analyst forecasts -> business
A celebrity announces a new sports team ownership -> sports (ownership/league) even though it is celebrity news
WHO declares a novel virus outbreak -> world (international health crisis), NOT science_technology unless the article is about the viral genome itself

A country passes a data-protection law -> world (foreign policy) or business (compliance)? Treat as 'world' if it is the political act; 'business' if the article is about firm impact. Specify: political act -> world
An esports tournament sponsor changes -> sports (esports), NOT business

A biotech drug gets FDA approval and the company stock jumps -> science_technology if the news is the approval/efficacy; business if the news is only the stock move. Default: efficacy/approval -> science_technology
Climate scientists warn of a specific regional flood; no policy, no market -> science_technology (climate science), not world
A stadium roof collapses injuring players -> sports (incident in a sporting venue) borderline world (tragedy); rule: venue-and-victims both in sports context -> sports
A new cryptocurrency exchange opens in a country -> business (markets), not science_technology (crypto as asset; not a tech breakthrough)
An AI company's earnings beat expectations -> business (results), NOT science_technology, even though the firm is AI
A foreign government nationalizes a tech company -> world (foreign political action dominant) NOT business
Empty or near-empty headline/summary -> other
business that looks like science_technology (it is business)
science_technology that looks like business (it is science_technology)
world that looks like business (it is world)
business that looks like world (it is business)

proposals.why: most confused: business->science_technology (56), science_technology->business (47), world->business (25), business->world (18); write targeted examples for these boundaries.
